title: Retrospective and Prospective Efficacy, Cost-Effectiveness, and Safety Analysis of Trabecular Micro-Bypass Surgery in Combination with Phacoemulsification—REKOSS Study
summary: In glaucoma, elevated intraocular pressure slowly damages the optic nerve and, if left untreated, can lead to blindness. If a patient is already scheduled for cataract surgery (clouding of the lens), a tiny implant or laser treatment can also improve the drainage of aqueous humor and thus lower intraocular pressure. This study examines how effectively this combination lowers intraocular pressure in routine clinical practice, whether it reduces the need for eye drops, how safe the treatment is, and what savings in medication costs it can yield. Patients who have received various implants or laser treatments will be compared with those who have undergone cataract surgery alone. This is purely an analysis of data that is collected anyway during medically necessary treatment; there are no additional examinations or treatments for the participants.

interventions.name: Phaco + iStent® infinite: Retrospective analysis with prospective collection of annual data of patients who underwent combined phacoemulsification and implantation of an iStent® infinite system, focusing on intraocular pressure, the number of glaucoma medications, and healthcare costs.

Phaco + iStent®: Retrospective analysis with prospective collection of annual data of patients who underwent combined phacoemulsification and implantation of an iStent® system (previous generation) with regard to intraocular pressure, the number of glaucoma medications, and healthcare costs.

Standalone Phaco: Retrospective analysis with prospective collection of annual data of patients who underwent phacoemulsification (cataract surgery) alone, without concomitant MIGS implantation, as a comparison/control group with regard to intraocular pressure, the number of glaucoma medications, an

Phaco + Elios®: Retrospective analysis with prospective collection of annual data of patients who underwent combined phacoemulsification and excimer laser trabeculostomy (Elios® system) with regard to intraocular pressure, the number of glaucoma medications, and healthcare costs.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group 1: Combined phacoemulsification and implantation of an iStent® infinite system at Sehwerk – Center for Ophthalmology during the defined study period.
Group 2: Combined phacoemulsification and implantation of an iStent® system at Sehwerk – Center for Ophthalmology during the defined study period. Group 3: Phacoemulsification alone without concomitant MIGS implantation at Sehwerk – Center for Ophthalmology during the defined study period.
Group 4: Combined phacoemulsification and excimer laser trabeculostomy (Elios® system) at Sehwerk – Center for Ophthalmology during the defined study period.
For all four groups: Presence of a confirmed diagnosis of glaucoma (primary open-angle glaucoma, pseudoexfoliation glaucoma) or ocular hypertension
